source.document: Volkswagen Body Repair Manual procedures — trigger language reproduced from VW repair manual as documented in Opus ADAS inspection reports. Per I-CAR, VW and Audi do not have separate scan/calibration position statements; requirements are specified within the body repair manual procedures.
source.note: Audi uses the same underlying VW Group service information structure. Calibration procedures and triggers are similar across the VW Group. SVM (Software Version Management) coding and programming is required for most modules when replaced.

general_requirements: VW/Audi calibrations require the factory-level scan tool (ODIS/VAS) and typically involve SVM coding and programming when modules are replaced. Targets are required for most camera and radar calibrations.

components.calibration_note: ADAS targets required for system calibration. SVM coding and programming required if module is replaced.
components.trigger_lead: The Adaptive Cruise Control / Front Assist Module requires SVM coding and programming if replaced. Calibration is required when any of the following apply:
triggers: Adaptive cruise control module / radar sensor is replaced
Radiator support is set to the service position
Adaptive cruise control module / radar sensor is removed and installed
Adjustments to the rear toe / thrust angle are made
Changes to the vehicle's ride height are made

components.calibration_note: ADAS targets required for system calibration. SVM coding and programming required if module is replaced.
components.trigger_lead: The Driver Assistance Front Camera control module requires SVM coding and programming if replaced. Calibration is required when any of the following apply:
triggers: No or incorrect basic setting / adaptation fault is stored in the event memory
Adjustments to the rear toe / thrust angle are performed
Repairs are made to the chassis that influence body height
Level control system sensor was readapted on vehicles with damping regulation
